'''Sophien Kamoun''' (Arabic: سفيان كمون; born 8 December 1965) is a [[Tunisia]]n [[biologist]]. He is a senior scientist at [[Sainsbury Laboratory|The Sainsbury Laboratory]] and [[professor]] of biology at the [[University of East Anglia]] (UEA). Kamoun is known for contributions to understanding [[plant diseases]] and [[plant immunity]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> He is a co-founder of Resurrect Bio<ref>{{Cite web |title=Team {{!}} Explore Our Expert Team - Join Us Now |url=https://www.resurrect.bio/team |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Resurrect Bio |language=en-GB}}</ref> and the nonprofit GetGenome<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Canham |first1=James |last2=Kamoun |first2=Sophien |title=Introducing GetGenome - Genomics for all! |url=https://zenodo.org/records/7186205 |journal=Zenodo |date=2022 |language=en |doi=10.5281/zenodo.7186205 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710092827/https://zenodo.org/records/7186205 |archive-date=2024-07-10}}</ref>, and he is a leading advocate of open science, preprints, and transparent peer review<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sophien |first=Kamoun |title=Embrace open science to empower your community and advance your career |url=https://zenodo.org/records/10391821 |journal=Zenodo |date=2023 |language=en |doi=10.5281/zenodo.10391821 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250717035036/https://zenodo.org/records/10391821 |archive-date=2025-07-17}}</ref>.

==Early life and education==
Kamoun grew up in Tunisia. He studied at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in Paris and then at the [[University of California, Davis]] where he obtained a [[PhD]] in 1991 for [[genetic analysis]] of [[pathogenicity]] of the bacteria, ''[[Xanthomonas campestris]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.apsnet.org/members/awards/Keen/Pages/KamounSophien.aspx |title=Keen Award: Sophien Kamoun |publisher=American Phytopathological Society |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref>

==Research and career==
[[File:Sophien Kamoun.jpg|alt=Sophien Kamoun|thumb|right|Kamoun in 2017]]
Kamoun is known for his contributions to understanding plant diseases and plant immunity. He used [[genomics]] and [[molecular biology]] methods to obtain insights into the biology and evolution of [[eukaryotic]] [[plant pathogen]]s.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/sophien-kamoun-13822/|title=Sophien Kamoun|website=Royalsociety.org|access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref> He discovered virulence effector families from plant pathogens and showed how they can modulate [[plant immunity]].<ref name=frs/> He demonstrated how antagonistic [[coevolution]] with host plants has impacted the architecture of pathogen genomes, accelerated the evolution of [[Plant disease resistance|effector genes]], and drove the emergence of [[immune receptor]] networks.<ref name=frs/>

After his PhD, Kamoun worked at the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) Center for Engineering Plants for Resistance Against Pathogens at the [[University of California, Davis]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=8920216 |title=NSF Award Search: Award#8920216 - Engineering Plants for Resistance Against Pathogens |website=Nsf.gov |access-date=2018-04-30}}{{failed verification|date=May 2018}}</ref> and at the Department of Phytopathology ([[Wageningen University]], Netherlands). He was on the faculty of the Department of Plant Pathology ([[Ohio State University]], Wooster campus) from 1998 to 2007, before joining [[Sainsbury Laboratory|The Sainsbury Laboratory]] in 2007. He served as Head of [[Sainsbury Laboratory|The Sainsbury Laboratory]] from 2009 to 2014<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-16 |title=Sophien Kamoun |url=https://www.tsl.ac.uk/about/people/sophien-kamoun |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=The Sainsbury Laboratory |language=en}}</ref> and also holds the rank of professor of biology at the [[University of East Anglia]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sophien Kamoun |url=https://research-portal.uea.ac.uk/en/persons/sophien-kamoun/ |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=University of East Anglia |language=en-GB}}</ref>. Kamoun served as president of the International Society for Molecular Plant-Microbe Interactions from 2012-2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ismpmi.org/About/Pages/History.aspx |title=History of the International Society for Molecular Plant-Microbe Interactions |publisher=International Society for Molecular Plant-Microbe Interactions |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Kamoun received several awards and recognitions. He received the 2003 Syngenta Award<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.apsnet.org/members/awards/Syngenta/Pages/default.aspx |title=Syngenta Award |publisher=American Phytopathological Society |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> and the 2013 Noel Keen Award from the American Phytopathological Society,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.apsnet.org/members/awards/Keen/Pages/default.aspx |title=Noel T. Keen Award for Research Excellence in Molecular Plant Pathology |publisher=American Phytopathological Society |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> the [[Daiwa Adrian Prize]] in 2010,<ref name=daiwa>{{cite web |title=Daiwa Adrian Prizes 2010 |url=http://dajf.org.uk/grants-awards-prizes/daiwa-adrian-prizes/daiwa-adrian-prizes-2010 |publisher=[[Daiwa Anglo-Japanese Foundation]] |access-date=2018-05-02}}</ref> and the Kuwait Prize in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kfas.org/Media-Publications/KFAS-News?NewsId=0d4f3707-6795-470d-be9e-ab1c61ae197a&MId= |title=KFAS announced the 2016 winners of the Kuwait Prize, the Scientific Production Prize, and Al-Nouri Prize for Best Ph.D. Thesis in Education |access-date=2018-04-30 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017042349/http://kfas.org/Media-Publications/KFAS-News?NewsId=0d4f3707-6795-470d-be9e-ab1c61ae197a&MId= |archive-date=2017-10-17 }}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (MAE) in 2011,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kamoun_Sophien |title=Academy of Europe: Sophien Kamoun |publisher=[[Academia Europaea]] |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> and the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 2015.<ref name=membo/><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.tsl.ac.uk/news/professor-sophien-kamoun-elected-embo-member/ |title=Professor Sophien Kamoun elected as EMBO member |work=TNews |publisher=The Sainsbury Laboratory |access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> Kamoun won successive [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advanced Investigator grants in 2011, 2017<ref>{{Cite news |title=ERC FUNDED PROJECTS |url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?search_api_views_fulltext=kamoun |access-date=2018-04-30 |publisher=European Research Council}}</ref> and in 2023 under the UK Horizon Europe Guarantee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GtR |url=https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=EP/Y032187/1 |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=gtr.ukri.org}}</ref> In 2018, he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name=frs/> and he received the [[Linnean Medal]] for his outstanding contributions to plant science.<ref name="lin1" /><ref name="lin2" /> He has been a Foreign Fellow of the Bangladesh Academy of Sciences since 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellow Details - Bangladesh Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.bas.org.bd/fellow-details/179 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=www.bas.org.bd}}</ref> As of 2025, Kamoun became a [[editor-in-chief|co-editor]] of the 
''[[Annual Review of Phytopathology]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Annual Review of Phytopathology -- Current editorial committee |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/phyto?page=editorial-committee |website=Annual Reviews |access-date=15 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
